issues.issue: "Net Eligible Revenue" is capitalised as a defined term but is nowhere defined in this Agreement, leaving the base against which adjustments are made unascertainable from the instrument. The size of the deduction turns on that undefined term.

This bullet says the employee arbitrates disputes with Wells Fargo Advisors "or a client, or any other person," while the operative clause, Paragraph 14(b), covers only controversies "arising between you and Wells Fargo Advisors." A court could be asked whether non-signatories may compel arbitration.

The exclusion is defined as claims "for State unemployment insurance" and then explained by an "i.e." list that includes workers' compensation and National Labor Relations Act claims, which are not state unemployment insurance. Whether the parenthetical narrows or enlarges the carve-out is genuinely uncertain.

The phrase "as provided by the rules of the arbitration forum in the claim is filed" is missing a word ("in which"), leaving the sentence ungrammatical. The defect is in a disclosure bullet rather than an operative term, so little turns on it.

The statement that "a claim that is ineligible for arbitration may be brought to court" sits against Paragraph 14(b), which routes any claim FINRA does not accept to the AAA rather than to court. A court could be asked which path an ineligible claim takes.

The covered-claims list ends with "federal, state or local statute or ordinance and/or other theory," a catch-all whose reach against the enumerated causes of action is uncertain. Whether a particular statutory claim falls inside is exactly the ejusdem generis question.

This clause reaches only disputes "arising between you and Wells Fargo Advisors," narrower than the Paragraph 14(a) disclosure that the employee arbitrates with "a client, or any other person." The two descriptions of scope cannot both be right.

The reservation of court injunctive relief for Wells Fargo alone is in tension with the Paragraph 14(a) disclosure that the employee gives up "the right to sue Wells Fargo Advisors ... in court concerning matters related to or arising from your employment." A court could be asked whether the carve-out is mutual.

This clause states that "indemnification obligations" survive, but the Agreement contains no indemnification provision — the nearest analogue is the Paragraph 13(a) contribution to settlements. What survives is therefore uncertain on the face of the instrument.

The clause directs that the Agreement "shall be deemed amended to the extent necessary" to save an unenforceable Provision without stating who performs the amendment or by what standard, and then contemplates that a court may decline to do so. The reformation mechanism's operation is open to argument, particularly as to the restrictive covenants.

The heading and acknowledgment refer to "the RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS" as a defined category, but no provision of the Agreement uses that label for Paragraphs 11 and 12. What the employee acknowledged is left to inference from the rest of the instrument.

The integration is limited to "the matters addressed herein," a qualifier that leaves the merger clause's reach uncertain where compensation plans and policies are involved. Which prior understandings are extinguished turns on that phrase.

An entire-agreement clause is difficult to reconcile with Paragraph 8's statement that the document is "only a synopsis" and with Paragraph 6's preservation of Wells Fargo human resources and compliance policies as binding. A court could be asked which of those governs.

"All provisions ... that require survival ... in order to give full legal effect thereto" is circular and identifies no particular obligation, so which terms survive is left at large. The phrase supplies no test a party could apply.

This open-ended survival language overlaps with Paragraph 15, which separately specifies that the confidentiality, post-employment and indemnification obligations survive, raising the question whether the enumeration there is exhaustive. The two survival clauses need to be harmonised.
